description: An enrolled relay whose certificate is still valid but has entered its renewal window renews ahead of expiry, without presenting a fresh claim credential: {csr} in, {cert, not_before, not_after} out, under the same relay_id. Per the REL-015 draft-note the exchange rides the Expired-certificate re-enrollment path's bootstrap transport until the in-band verb lands — eligibility there is issuance-record-based, never expiry-gated, so the unexpired most-recently-issued certificate renews identically. The CSR is over the SAME keypair the current certificate certifies (REL-015 mandates no rotation; the key is the player-pinned trust anchor), so the renewed certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo is byte-identical. Afterward the app peer's issuance record shows the fresh serial as most-recently-issued; the prior certificate is SUPERSEDED — re-presenting it for renewal draws CERT_EXPIRED_INELIGIBLE (REL-021/022) — but it is NOT thereby revoked (REL-016), so an established connection that authenticated with it continues undisturbed until its own natural end.
